chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) he said: Hadeethani (narrated to me) Hakim ibn Dawud from Salamah ibn al-Khattab from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Mu'alla from Isḥaq ibn Dawud who said:

A man came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him: 'I have placed a mark on all my belongings of gold and silver, and I sold my rural estates, so I said: I will settle in Mecca.' He said: 'Do not do so, for the people of Mecca disbelieve in God openly.' I said: 'Then in the sanctuary of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family)?' He said: 'They are worse than them.' I said: 'Then where should I settle?' He said: 'You should go to Iraq, to Kufa, for the blessing from it is for twelve miles, thus and thus, and next to it is a grave; any distressed person who visits it, or any grieving person, God will relieve his distress.'

key_terms.حَرَمِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The sanctuary of the Messenger of God (referring to Medina)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq advise against settling in Mecca and recommend Kufa instead?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) contrasts the spiritual decline of Mecca and Medina with the enduring sanctity of Kufa, a city deeply tied to the Ahl al-Bayt. He specifically highlights a grave within two miles of Kufa—widely interpreted by Shia scholars as that of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib or a revered companion—promising divine relief for those who visit in times of distress. This recommendation underscores Kufa's status as a central hub of Shia piety and a place of spiritual refuge during periods of political and religious turmoil.
